rounds.direction: Explore depot-aware savings and capacity-aware alternatives to nearest-neighbor CVRP construction.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 5 was best at 11.56280 versus 12.11504 for nearest neighbor. It maximizes a savings score with a demand multiplier. The direct closure-cost variants in this round were worse, and its savings are all zero at the depot.

rounds.direction: Separate route start from in-route savings.
rounds.assessment: Both explicit-start candidates were valid but worse than 11.56280. Candidate 1 used a farthest-depot anchor and also increased demand weights, so the effect of the anchor alone is unresolved. Its instance 0 rose to 13.05925 from 10.19858.

rounds.direction: Test capacity pressure while retaining the incumbent route-start behavior.
rounds.assessment: The valid blended distance and residual-fill score regressed to 12.73959. Candidate 2 used local-frontier scoring plus a depot-return gate and failed invalid_route. The run does not isolate fill from other changes.

rounds.direction: Recover a clean ranking comparison after the invalid route.
rounds.assessment: Both candidates remained valid and retained the incumbent savings expression. The best multiplied savings by a penalty for leftover capacity far from mean feasible demand, scoring 12.03830; the incumbent stayed at 11.56280.

rounds.direction: Explore one-step capacity-feasible continuation to distinguish geographically similar moves.
rounds.assessment: Both generated candidates attempted a continuation heuristic but were rejected before scoring: candidate 1 used forbidden np.empty and candidate 2 used forbidden np.linspace. There is no distance evidence against lookahead itself.

rounds.direction: Make the one-step continuation hypothesis evaluable.
rounds.assessment: Both revised lookahead candidates were evaluable, scoring 13.14740 and 14.15724. The better one shortlists by current distance and reranks via continuation and depot distance, replacing the incumbent ordering. These implementations did not justify further complex lookahead yet.

rounds.direction: Pivot to geometric cohesion using the depot as the origin.
rounds.assessment: The cosine-alignment savings variant reduced the incumbent to 11.29829. It improved instances 1, 3 and 4 and regressed on 0, 2 and 5. It also lowered the demand bonus, so the gain cannot be assigned to angle alone.

rounds.direction: Explore adaptive directional strength while preserving the new savings skeleton.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 2 softened cosine alignment using the feasible-set size and capacity pressure. Its mean improved to 11.11117, chiefly through instances 0 and 5, while instances 3 and 4 regressed. Candidate 1 regressed to 12.20259.

rounds.direction: Revisit the degenerate depot start without reverting the improved in-route policy.
rounds.assessment: The two cluster-aware start proposals were rejected before route scoring. The reported disallowed attributes were ix_ and fill_diagonal, so the outcome cannot assess the start heuristic.

rounds.direction: Make a cluster-aware depot start evaluable with one row at a time.
rounds.assessment: Both cluster-anchor variants scored. The best minimizes depot distance plus half the nearest-peer distance at route start and also changes in-route weights. It improved instances 0 and 1 but regressed on 2–5; mean 11.37520 did not displace 11.11117.

rounds.direction: Explore radial progression inside a route.
rounds.assessment: The best radial variant retained the incumbent formula and multiplied by a small factor containing radial distance divided by remaining capacity. It scored 11.14047, unchanged on four instances and worse on 3 and 5; the other variant scored 12.44891.

rounds.direction: Use a dimensionless radial feature with a narrow effect on near-ties.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 was rejected on a disallowed attribute. Candidate 2 used a dimensionless detour correction but fell back to nearest-current distance as its base, scoring 12.09879; five instance scores exactly matched nearest neighbor. This leaves the intended near-tie modification to adaptive savings unverified.

rounds.direction: Explore scale-normalized savings directly rather than reverting to nearest neighbor.
rounds.assessment: Both scale-normalized savings variants were valid. Candidate 2 scored 11.38412, better on instances 1–3 but worse on 0, 4 and 5. It normalized by radius sum plus savings and also added a distance tie break, so normalization alone is not isolated.

rounds.direction: Explore a narrow mix of absolute and normalized savings.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 2 improved to 11.06360. It used raw savings to shortlist within 2% of the leader and then normalized savings minus a demand penalty, dropping angular alignment. Instances 1, 2 and 5 improved while 0, 3 and 4 regressed. This is a useful deviation from the submitted Plan.

rounds.direction: Refine the verified two-stage savings shortlist.
rounds.assessment: Both candidates used the two-stage family and neither improved the incumbent. Candidate 1 narrowed the window from 2% to 1% and raised the penalty from 0.10 to 0.25; its mean was 11.08590. Its only strict per-instance improvement was on instance 4.

rounds.direction: Combine the two successful ideas only inside the near-tie set.
rounds.assessment: Both candidates returned exactly the round-14 incumbent's per-instance distance vector. Candidate 1 added a weak angular term only in the near-tie secondary score and left the depot term zero. Identical distances on these six instances do not identify the full routes or prove decision equivalence.

rounds.direction: Explore route cohesion before adding lookahead.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 6 beat the nearest-neighbor baseline at 11.59109. Its formula reduces algebraically to distance minus 0.20 times demand fill times depot distance when the radial maximum is positive. The selected code contains no angular term.

rounds.direction: Use the simplified incumbent as the reference and add a small directional signal.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 2 reached 11.41894 but did not implement angle. Away from the depot its ordering is equivalent to minimizing d_current - 0.85*d_depot + 0.10*dmax*fill. Four instances improved versus the round-1 incumbent and two regressed.

rounds.direction: Keep the normalized-savings primary ranking and test a near-tie correction.
rounds.assessment: Both near-tie candidates were rejected for np.count_nonzero. This round did not measure whether near-tie angular guidance helps.

rounds.direction: Make the near-tie mechanism evaluable.
rounds.assessment: Both candidates became evaluable after switching away from count_nonzero. Candidate 1 reached 11.39272 by ranking savings divided by current distance before a radial/fill tie-break. That changes the primary score, and instances 3 and 4 became worse.

rounds.direction: Refine the actual two-stage ratio winner, targeting the two expensive instances.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 improved to 11.06980 and beat nearest neighbor on all six instances. It replaced the intended two-stage near-tie adjustment with a global product of normalized savings, quadratic fill and radial preference.

rounds.direction: Treat the global product winner as the reference for a small refinement.
rounds.assessment: One candidate was rejected on an unsupported attribute. The valid candidate kept the product but changed both fill and radial coefficients with the same taper; it scored 11.20186. The evidence does not isolate fill.

rounds.direction: Probe a radial coefficient change with the winner otherwise held fixed.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 remained legal but scored 34.70187. It renamed the positive depot savings term detour and minimized it, reversing its preference. Candidate 2 retained the maximizing product and scored 11.28541. The 11.06980 incumbent remains.

rounds.direction: Protect the direction of positive savings while exploring one local correction.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 switched from the incumbent product to additive savings with square-root fill, scoring 11.59534. Candidate 2 was rejected for an unsupported attribute. Neither displaced the round-5 winner.

rounds.direction: Explore incremental route closure cost with a focused capacity tie-break.
rounds.assessment: Five candidates were valid, and the best closure-cost and fill variant scored 12.29975, worse than 12.11504. It improved instances 0, 4 and 5 but regressed on the other three.

rounds.direction: Decompose depot closure and test the cost of over-weighting the return leg.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 retained a positive depot term and scored 12.54102. Candidate 2 failed invalid_route. Across two rounds the valid positive-return-leg variants have not beaten nearest neighbor.

rounds.direction: Pivot from positive return-leg costs to a depot savings signal.
rounds.assessment: The valid candidate uses d_current - 0.60*d_depot with a tiny demand tie-break. It improved all six instances versus the nearest-neighbor baseline and averaged 11.08588. The other candidate was rejected for count_nonzero.

rounds.direction: Refine the radial attraction while keeping the simple winning score.
rounds.assessment: The adaptive radial coefficient scored 11.17763, with improvements on instances 2 and 3 but regressions on 0, 4 and 5. It also altered the depot branch, so the capacity adjustment alone remains unresolved.

rounds.direction: Keep the proven linear score and add direction only as a small tie correction.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 retained the linear score and gated a weak angular term on a near tie. The mean moved from 11.08588 to 11.08119, entirely due to instance 4. The actual cosine is measured at the current customer, not at the depot.

rounds.direction: Explore a distance-scaled capacity tie-break around the linear winner.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 improved to 10.91967. It retained the 0.60 radial term, added a residual-capacity penalty divided by current distance when near ties existed, and then compared every candidate. A node outside the mask can therefore win. The main gain is on instance 2; instances 4 and 5 regressed.

rounds.direction: Test a capacity tie-break with a strict shortlist boundary.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 2 enforced the near-tie mask during selection and capped the capacity penalty. It scored 10.95699; the other candidate failed at runtime. The strict implementation did not beat the more permissive round-6 winner, and the cap is a second change.

rounds.direction: Refine the actual round-6 winner without assuming strict masking helps.
rounds.assessment: Candidate 1 replaced the planned linear score with normalized current distance plus an explicit depot-angle cost, scoring 11.28546. Candidate 2 also regressed, to 17.24785. The round-6 winner remains.
